title: Unit Event — Walk on and on — Episode3 A Sampling Lesson!

meta.Event Outline: In preparation for their next event, Vivid BAD SQUAD, Arata and the others set out to write different songs based on a single theme. Akito and An take on the duty of making the new track, but Toya wishes that he could contribute to lighten their load.

rows.Line: A few days later
Hospital

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I'm eager to get started today, Soma.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Haha. You're so old-fashioned. It's no biggie. I'm just giving you a few tips regarding sampling.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: No, I need to properly show my appreciation since I'll be taking up so much of your time with this.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I get how you feel, but let's just try to have fun, okay? Anyway, let's get started!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: By the way, Aoyagi, you already know a thing or two about sampling, right?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh, yes. I know a little bit.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: You take existing sounds, phrases and whatnot from existing songs, and create new works out of them, yes?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah, that's right. To be more precise, it's not just songs. You can use sounds from the natural world, people, machines... Anything that creates noise, really.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: However, you're pretty much spot on when it comes to street music, Aoyagi.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Is this how you've always made your own songs, Soma?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: No, I started doing this for the very first time after I got into street music.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I wanted to learn as much as I could about the culture surrounding street music, and sampling became a part of that.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Oh, speaking of culture, you mentioned something the other day that caught my attention.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Hm? I did?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah, the thing about having a background in classical music keeping you from fully understanding sampling and street music culture.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Why would knowing how to play classical music make things more difficult?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Ah, well...
This has to sort of do with my own feeling.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: When I was still playing classical music, my dad taught me to give absolute respect to each note of a piece of sheet music.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: He was adamant about understanding the motives of the composer and playing said music the way they originally intended.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: On the other hand, sampling involves using snippets of songs. You're essentially doing the opposite of what the creator intended, which I seem to have trouble dealing with...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: For instance, my dad once said that it would make sense if one were to use an entire movement from another composer's work, like Chopin did.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Yeah, I understand.
That would make the process of picking and modifying one part of a song kinda hard.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: At the same time, in my mind, sampling is actually really similar to what you just described.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Huh? What do you mean?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: At its core, sampling involves properly respecting the works that others have made.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: You borrow the parts of songs that you want to use, but if you don't know how to use them effectively, it ends up being a pointless exercise.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: You sorta need to be open about how it's influenced you. Only then can you create something that's new and reflects who you are.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I see. I never thought of it that way...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah, songwriting's interesting because you can look at it from so many different angles.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Also, it's really cool to hear about how much you studied classical music!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh, um... My dad's a classical pianist and a composer...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Wait, what?! That's incredible!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Life wasn't easy since he was a very strict teacher...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But thanks to you, Soma, I was able to discover the connection between classical and street music. It's put me at ease.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Alright, since we've sorta laid your fears to rest, why don't we give it a go...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: You write songs on your laptop?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Yup.
This is the one I used when Arata and I still sang together.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: And here are all the audio files that I was collecting until four years ago. They're all in this sampling folder.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Oh, there are so many!
This one's titled... “Crowd”?
And this one's “Underpass”?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah, I like to use snippets of existing songs, but I also enjoy using sounds you can hear from the world around us.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
I see...
And there seems to be more. Cracking an egg open, the sound of slippers and other things from regular life...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Haha. I guess you can chalk it up to me interpreting all these sounds as music.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Also, by using these kinds of sounds, you can tie your music to day-to-day life.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Hehe...
That's a nice way to think about it.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Isn't it? Since you're saying that, let's try putting a song together!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Well, that's what I want to say...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: But I can only use one of my hands right now, so typing and stuff's a bit of a challenge. Thanks for taking over...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: No, this is the least I could do since you're going out of your way to teach me.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Now, let's start by choosing a beat.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Right. We can't begin unless we do that.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: We'll need a base sound... What should we use?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Oh, I know.
There's this song I listened to a lot on my way to school. We can try creating a beat by looping its intro.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: To me, this song says, “You may not feel great now, but something good will happen tomorrow.” It's really uplifting and always found a way to cheer me up.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: This song must mean quite a lot to you, Soma.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Yeah, it does.
Listening to it in the morning gets me so pumped up!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: So, we can try making a song that encapsulates a fun and happy morning. Once we've finished inputting everything for the bass and drums, let's move on to phrases...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: A sax should help jazz things up and make it sound more hip. Also, it might be fun to throw in an acoustic guitar somewhere.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: That's what's great about all this. You can express yourself however you like and just go with what you feel when you hear these sounds. It doesn't matter if something personal comes to mind either.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Something personal... Does that mean you'd try using some of those sounds from day-to-day life here, Soma?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Hey, you're pretty sharp.
Yeah, I'd probably toss in the sounds of some dishes clinking or birds chirping.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Oh, but Arata would usually say, “These clash too much with the other sounds,” when I got a bit overzealous...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I see... I will bear that in mind.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Um... Toya, by the way...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Why do you seem so determined to write your own songs?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: This is just based on my own experience, but I feel that good performances are what get a crowd going.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: So, I really don't think you need to focus so much on writing your own stuff. If Shinonome's good at that, then I feel you can just leave it to him.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Aoyagi?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Akito said that I should just keep trying until I feel satisfied...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Which means he's willing to wait until I finish my song.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But I can't make him wait forever.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Azusawa started singing not too long ago and is growing at a tremendous pace. She has a natural talent for it and surprises me every time we perform together.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Shiraishi has guts and is very good at interacting with the audience. Every musician in town admires her very much.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: And Akito has this uncanny perception when on stage. He's able to monitor what's going on during a performance and support the rest of us while keeping his foot on the gas pedal.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Right...
Arata's told me all about Vivid BAD SQUAD. You guys are all such powerful performers and seem to really care about one another.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, I can always count on them for help...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Which is also the reason why I can't make them wait more than they need to. I want to show them some good results.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I want to be more of a contributor...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: When it comes to singing and performing, I feel confident about keeping up with the others now. However...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I can't help but be bothered by the things I'm still now able to do. Am I asking for too much...?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
No, I don't think so.
That's just how life is, right?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, well...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
You too, huh, Aoyagi...?
You wanna be more of a contributor...

rows.Speaker: Nurse
rows.Line: Excuse me, Mr. Miyata.

rows.Speaker: Soma & Toya
rows.Line: Huh?

rows.Speaker: Nurse
rows.Line: Oh, you have a friend visiting.

rows.Speaker: Nurse
rows.Line: I'm sorry, Mr. Miyata, would you mind coming with me? It's time for that test...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Oh, that's right!
I completely forgot that I was supposed to do that today!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Sorry, Aoyagi, I need to go for a bit! I'll be back in like thirty minutes!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: O-Okay... Um...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Oh, right. You won't have much to do while I'm gone. I know. You can try listening to the other sounds on my laptop!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: They should all be in the folder at the very top!

rows.Speaker: Nurse
rows.Line: Alright, we really need to get going.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Again, sorry! I'll be right back!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
I feel kind of bad...
I didn't realize that he had to do a test today.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But I have some time on my hands now. What should I do...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Soma said that there were more sounds in that folder. Is it this? The newest one...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Hm? It was last used yesterday?
These songwriting tools also seem to have been used fairly recently.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: He said that I could listen to them, so I guess I'll take him up on his offer and...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
*Gasp*
This song...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Sorry about that, Aoyagi!
It went by quicker than expected.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Wait, that song...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh, Soma...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: This is the incomplete song that Tono showed us. Were you working on it just recently?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Oh, wait... The very top...
Okay, that was my mistake. Of course you'd find it...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: But you're right...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Remember how you said you want to be more of a contributor, Aoyagi? I feel the same way.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I want to help Arata as much as I can, and I decided to finish the track I was working on before my accident.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
For Arata...
Yes, I see.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Um, Soma...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I really enjoyed the new parts you've been working on too. They feel so free, liberating and harsh, but also kind.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: They're a wonderful expression of your courageous nature and sensitivity...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I would be very envious of the person who got to sing this track.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: What...?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Ohh. Haha...
You have this way of catching me off guard whenever I talk to you, Aoyagi.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: It's just... You were so straight with me that I feel a bit stupid for being awkward...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I'm slightly embarrassed by what you said, but I also really appreciate it. So, thanks!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Unfortunately, I haven't really been getting anywhere with it, and I'm not really sure when I'll be able to finish it.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Is it giving you that much trouble?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah, not being able to move my body around freely has something to do with it...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: But remember how I said Arata and I used to work on stuff together?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Ah, yes, I remember.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I prefer to create as I go based on how I feel, but Arata's the logical type. It doesn't matter that he isn't great at coming up with phrases since he is good at putting things in the right order.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Which is why it took both of us to create a song from start to finish.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Ah, that explains why Tono said you were the one who wrote that song...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: To be fair, it sounds like he can do just about anything on his own now...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: The truth is, I wish that I could write entire songs on my own...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Um, Aoyagi, can I ask you for a favor...?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Every so often, could you stop by to give me your take on things like you did just now?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, of course, but my opinions? Are you sure?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah, I'm sure. Arata and I used to discuss which sound is best for a given part, and that always helped a lot.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: But I sorta get lost when I have to write songs all on my own like this. That's why I need to hear from someone else. Only then will I know how I'm really doing.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: If you're okay with me being that person...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
But why me...?
Can't you just make them again with Tono...?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: No, I'd like it if you didn't tell him about this...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: What?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: For Arata's sake, as well as mine, I want to finish this song. I don't know if I'll be able to make it right, but I really want to avoid disappointing him by not doing so.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Which is why I don't want him knowing what I'm doing right now. If possible, can you not tell anyone else about this?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Understood.
I won't tell Arata, Akito or anybody else.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Thanks, that helps a lot...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
No, it's okay.
I can tell that you care deeply about this song.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Yeah. I wanna finish it someday and hand it over to him.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: (Hand it over someday...)

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I know how you feel, Soma, since I also have teammates that I care very much about.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I also wish to be there for them as much as possible.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Aoyagi...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Um, Soma. You asked me to give you my thoughts, but is there anything else I can do to help?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I'm also not very good at coming up with phrases and such, but I think I can assist you by adjusting sounds and arranging everything.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: No, I shouldn't take up more of your time. I mean, you still have to get ready for that event, right?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I know how serious all of you guys are about it, so I don't want to get in the way of you succeeding.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
No, that won't be an issue.
I have every reason to help you right now, Soma.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Every reason...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes. They say learning by doing is best, and I stand to benefit and learn quite a by watching the way you write songs.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I'd like to make some progress as well. So, Soma, will you be willing to help me with that?

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Help you...?
I wasn't expecting to hear that.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Okay, got it.
Alright, Aoyagi, I'll lend you a hand.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
...!
Thank you very much!

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line:
Sure thing, but...
Let's hold off on working together until just before you guys' event.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Wait, but...

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: I honestly don't know how long this is gonna take, so I can't really ask you to stay with me until I do.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: But it'll be like us trading this for that. You'll help me with my track and I'll help you learn as much as I can about songwriting. How's that sound?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Okay, I understand...
I'll be looking forward to working with you prior to our next event.

rows.Speaker: Soma
rows.Line: Thanks, Aoyagi! I'll be looking forward to your help!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes, I'm looking forward to helping as well.
